faq.ariaLabel: Frequently asked questions about choosing a festival
faq.title: Questions that usually come up before your first festival
faq.description: A quick layer of context to decide better: which genre fits, where to compare dates, and when to jump to the official site before buying.

tickets.question: Can I buy tickets directly on TuriaFestNoticias?
tickets.answer: No. TuriaFestNoticias works as an editorial guide: it helps you compare festivals, dates and venues, then takes you to each event's official link to complete your purchase.

genres.question: Can I discover festivals by music style?
genres.answer: Yes. The home page, calendar and festival pages are designed to orient you quickly across electronic, urban, pop and Latin without blindly opening every festival.

provinces.question: How do I compare Valencia, Alicante and Castellón?
provinces.answer: Use the home page as your starting point: first the editorial calendar, then the Valencian Community map, and from there jump to the festivals that best match your location.

family.question: How do I know if a festival suits a group or family trip?
family.answer: Each festival page summarises the event tone, location and type of experience. For exact age policies, access rules or companions, the final step is always the official website.

details.question: Where do I check line-up, venue and practical details before deciding?
details.answer: Every festival has its own TuriaFestNoticias page with editorial context, dates, map and direct access to the official site, where you'll find the confirmed line-up, schedules and final rules.

dates.question: What if I want to plan my summer by dates first?
dates.answer: Start with the calendar: it shows festivals in chronological order so you can jump to the event page once you know which weekend you want to book.

overview.paragraph1: Bigsound Festival has established itself as one of the leading pop and indie events in the Valencian Community. Hosted at Parc Central de Torrent, it pairs international headliners with emerging Spanish artists and delivers a polished production aimed at a multi-generational audience.
overview.paragraph2: Two days of live music, Mediterranean food trucks and chill zones tuned to the Valencian summer. Easy public-transport access from downtown and a side programme of activities that kicks off in the afternoon.

overview.paragraph1: Latin Fest is the reference festival for reggaeton and Latin urban music in the Valencian Community. Tight lineup of major names in the genre and a production designed for a young crowd looking for spectacle, dance and Mediterranean energy.
overview.paragraph2: The main venue is in Valencia city, usually paired with a stop in Benidorm. Easy public-transport access, hydration zones, Latin food trucks and a festive summer atmosphere.

posterGallery.title: Official Posters
posterGallery.intro: The main festival poster and its city variations so each edition can be compared at a glance.

overview.paragraph1: Medusa Festival is one of the most important electronic music festivals in Europe and a must-watch highlight of the Spanish summer. Held on the spectacular beach of Cullera, Valencia, it brings together some of the best international DJs and artists for five days in a unique setting by the Mediterranean Sea.
overview.paragraph2: With more than 300,000 m² of venue space, spectacular themed stages, large-format audiovisual production, and an unmatched immersive experience, Medusa Festival attracts thousands of attendees from all over the world every year in search of music, spectacle, and an unforgettable atmosphere.

posterGallery.title: Official Posters
posterGallery.intro: The main poster and the day-by-day visual line-up so the whole week can be scanned at a glance.

overview.paragraph1: Arenal Sound turns Burriana into one of the Mediterranean summer's major festival meeting points. Four days by Playa del Arenal with a broad mix of pop, urban music and electronic sets.
overview.paragraph2: The festival combines live shows, DJ sessions, rest areas, camping and a programme built for moving between stages all day. Its Castellón coast location makes it an easy pick for a beach-and-music trip.

posterGallery.title: Official Arenal Sound 2026 poster
posterGallery.intro: The poster brings together pop, urban and electronic names for the Burriana edition.

overview.paragraph1: Reve Festival is the night-time pop highlight of the Valencian summer, with a mainstream-oriented lineup and large-format visual spectacle. Built for large audiences, it prioritises staging and sound quality over the classic open-air festival formula.
overview.paragraph2: Located at Roig Arena, it offers a comfortable experience with strong public-transport access, nearby hotels, food zones, and audiovisual productions that stretch the night until late.

overview.paragraph1: Zevra Festival is an urban and Latin experience held by the Mediterranean, on Cullera beach (Valencia). Four days with a lineup centered on reggaeton, latin and urban, in a venue designed to combine music, beach, and summer party.
overview.paragraph2: Large-scale production, multiple stages, Mediterranean and Latin food-truck zones, and an afterparty calendar that extends to nearby clubs. Easy drive from Valencia city.

latinFestValencia2026.title: Latin Fest fills Valencia with urban music for two days
latinFestValencia2026.summary: Latin Fest debuted its two-day format at Estadi Ciutat de València. Beéle, ROA and Kris R shaped Friday; Mora, Omar Courtz, Kapo and Pirlo took over on Saturday.
latinFestValencia2026.searchGenres: latin urban music reggaeton latin trap afrobeat dancehall latin pop
latinFestValencia2026.seoTitle: Latin Fest Valencia: two days of urban music | TuriaFest
latinFestValencia2026.seoDescription: Latin Fest debuted two days at Estadi Ciutat de València with Beéle, ROA, Kris R, Mora, Omar Courtz, Kapo and Pirlo.
latinFestValencia2026.coverAlt: A Latin Fest artist sings in a white hat in front of a red-lit stage
latinFestValencia2026.coverCaption: Latin Fest brought two days of urban music to Estadi Ciutat de València on 17 and 18 July.
latinFestValencia2026.highlight: By expanding from a single date to two days, Latin Fest gave each line-up its own rhythm without losing the sense of one shared celebration.

newStage.heading: A stadium opens a new chapter
newStage.paragraph1: Latin Fest began an edition unlike any of its previous Valencia dates on 17 July. The festival left Auditorio Marina Sur behind, moved into Estadi Ciutat de València and expanded its programme across two consecutive days.
newStage.paragraph2: Each day ran from five in the afternoon until one in the morning. The stadium format gave the visuals, dance ensemble and live bands more depth, while DJ sets connected the concerts and kept the momentum going between stage changes.

friday.heading: Friday: three voices launch the new format
friday.paragraph1: Beéle, ROA and Kris R carried the first date. The line-up moved between Caribbean melodies, reggaeton and trap without treating Friday as a warm-up: the day had an identity of its own from the opening hours through the night-time stretch.
friday.paragraph2: The production followed that journey with constant colour changes, large-format screens and live musicians. Between performances, the DJs kept the floor moving and prevented the energy from having to restart at every handover.

saturday.heading: Saturday: the handover raises the intensity
saturday.paragraph1: The second day brought a new cast with Mora, Omar Courtz, Kapo and Pirlo. Their performances broadened the festival's range from urban pop and Afro-Caribbean rhythms to Puerto Rican and Colombian reggaeton and trap.
saturday.paragraph2: As night fell, the staging grew in scale: large inflatables, beams of light sweeping across the audience and a visual production that occupied the entire back of the stadium. Saturday completed a weekend that made Latin Fest's expansion more than a sequence of concerts: two distinct days within one urban-music gathering.

reveFest2026.title: Reve Fest debuts in Valencia with urban music for hospitals
reveFest2026.summary: The festival opened its first edition with six live sets and several DJ sessions. Proceeds will support new Músicos por la Salud micro-concerts in hospitals and social-healthcare centres.
reveFest2026.searchGenres: urban music reggaeton trap urban pop latin
reveFest2026.seoTitle: Reve Fest debuts with urban music for a cause | TuriaFest
reveFest2026.seoDescription: Reve Fest debuts at Roig Arena with six artists and proceeds dedicated to bringing micro-concerts into hospitals.
reveFest2026.coverAlt: A Reve Fest artist sings on the Roig Arena stage under violet lights
reveFest2026.coverCaption: Reve Fest brought nine hours of urban music to Roig Arena on 16 July.
reveFest2026.highlight: What happened during one afternoon in Valencia will continue later in hospitals and social-healthcare centres through new micro-concerts.

debut.heading: A first edition with two destinations
debut.paragraph1: Reve Fest debuted at Roig Arena on 16 July with a two-part idea: bring different voices from the urban scene together for nine hours, then allow the result of the day to continue long after the stage went dark.
debut.paragraph2: Thousands of attendees, most of them young, joined the festival's Valencia debut. Six performances and several DJ sessions formed one continuous programme conceived as a journey through distinct urban styles.

lineup.heading: A line-up moving between scenes
lineup.paragraph1: Kidd Voodoo brought a stop on his Euphoria World Tour to Valencia. The handover then went to C. Marí and his blend of reggaeton, trap and contemporary sounds before Lorna completed the first part of the event.
lineup.paragraph2: María Becerra opened the second half with her Latin urban-pop repertoire. La Zowi shifted the tone towards trap and RVFV took charge of the finale. Between each live set, DJ sessions kept the music moving and connected artists with very different identities.

purpose.heading: The proceeds move to another stage
purpose.paragraph1: What sets Reve Fest apart becomes clear after the final concert. Músicos por la Salud, the organisation behind the event, will use the proceeds to hire young performers for its small-format concerts in hospitals and social-healthcare centres.
purpose.paragraph2: The first edition is therefore connected to work that takes place far from major venues. The audience discovered a new urban-music date in Valencia while also helping music reach people who will experience it in a completely different setting.
